configurations.name: servicenowUrl
configurations.description: The URL of your ServiceNow instance. This should be the address you use to access the ServiceNow UI in your browser. For example, `https://dev12345.service-now.com`

configurations.name: servicenowUsername
configurations.description: The username of the ServiceNow account for Basic authentication. Not required if using OAuth Client Credentials. To create user credentials, see the ServiceNow documentation

configurations.name: servicenowPassword
configurations.description: The password of the ServiceNow account for Basic authentication. Not required if using OAuth Client Credentials. To create user credentials, see the ServiceNow documentation

configurations.name: servicenowClientId
configurations.description: OAuth Client ID for Client Credentials authentication. To configure OAuth, see the ServiceNow OAuth documentation

configurations.name: servicenowClientSecret
configurations.description: OAuth Client Secret for Client Credentials authentication. To configure OAuth, see the ServiceNow OAuth documentation

configurations.name: enableTablesLiveEventsWebhooks
configurations.description: Enable automatic creation of Business Rules in ServiceNow for real-time events forwarding to Port. When enabled, business rules are created for every table in your mapping configuration, or only for tables specified in `liveEventTables`.

configurations.name: liveEventTables
configurations.description: Optional list of specific table names to configure for live events. If not specified but enableTablesLiveEventsWebhooks is true, all tables from the mapping configuration will be configured. Use this to limit which tables trigger live events.

configurations.name: webhookSecret
configurations.description: A secret token used to authenticate incoming webhook requests from ServiceNow. When configured, the integration will automatically add this as an Authorization header on the outbound REST Message in ServiceNow and validate it on incoming requests.
